newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Retired Romania officer seeks damages from Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Retired Romania officer seeks damages from Clinton.

text.p: A retired army officer is seeking $20,000 in damages from visiting U.S. President Bill Clinton for being denied promotion by communists after saving the life of a American pilot, a Romanian daily said on Friday.
"I hope Clinton has the money with him. If he has no time to meet me, he can leave it with (Romanian President Emil) Constantinescu," Colonel Eugen Zahiu told Evenimentul Zilei.

Zahiu, 75, said the money covered 50 years of lost wages when communist authorities refused to promote him because he had saved the life of an American pilot in 1944 as head of a military unit defending Bucharest.
At the outbreak of the war, Romania was governed by the fascist "Iron Guard" which allied itself with Nazi Germany, but it switched sides in August 1944 to join the Allies.

Zahiu said he had long forgiven the United States for Romania falling into the communist sphere of influence after the war. But Clinton, he said, owed him compensation for resisting early Romanian membership of NATO.

"My whole life I had to suffer for having loved the Americans," he said. "Now that they have rejected Romania for the first NATO wave, I don't know if I will live long enough to catch the next wave, I decided to ask for my money now."

Clinton, the first U.S President to visit the ex-communist country in 22 years, led resistance to including Romania in NATO's first expansion. A NATO summit this week invited only Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic for early membership.
